title: The Election Won’t Stop THIS (Most Aren’t Ready)
creator: MarketBeat
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: MarketBeat hosts a guest from Real Alloys to explain the 1 January 2027 DFARS deadline, after which no Chinese-origin or embargoed-country metals may go into US defence systems — no F-35s, submarines or aircraft carriers with Chinese-origin metals or magnets. The problem is scale: over 90% of light rare earths, 97% of heavy rare earths and over 90% of magnets are made in China, while US magnet output is only about 500 tons a year against roughly 50,000 tons of demand. The guest says the deadline has bipartisan support and will not change with the election, that the administration has warned monthly, and that defence firms have stockpiled enough for a few months — but a shortage thereafter is inevitable without domestic build-out. Building that capacity is a 7–10 year journey, he says, and his firm starts rare-earth metal production in the first quarter of next year, including heavy rare earths where the US currently produces nothing, from an Army-base site in Utah. His message to investors is long-term only: reshoring is an irreversible trend with or without the deadline, but he explicitly says 'we don't speculate on near-term stock prices'. MP Materials is mentioned only factually as the one US light-rare-earth processor with no heavy rare earths, and Real Alloys is discussed as the guest's own company, so no stock call-event is recorded.
